```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# cache results
knitr::opts_chunk$set(cache=TRUE, message=FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
```
In this data challenge we explore the qualities of diamonds and their association with price using the `ggplot2::diamonds` dataset:

1. First of all, observe that low quality diamonds (with respect to cut, color and clarity) are more expensive.

```{r}
# price by cut: Fair (worst) has a higher median than Ideal (best)
ggplot(data = diamonds) +
  geom_boxplot(mapping = aes(x = cut, y = price)) +
  labs(x = "cut (worst → best)", y = "price (USD)")

# price by color: J (worst) has the highest median
ggplot(data = diamonds) +
  geom_boxplot(mapping = aes(x = color, y = price)) +
  labs(x = "color (best → worst)", y = "price (USD)")

# price by clarity: I1 (worst) has a higher median than IF (best)
ggplot(data = diamonds) +
  geom_boxplot(mapping = aes(x = clarity, y = price)) +
  labs(x = "clarity (worst → best)", y = "price (USD)")
```

2. Using models, find an explanation and solve the apparent paradox.

```{r}
ggplot(data = diamonds) +
  geom_boxplot(mapping = aes(x = cut, y = carat))

ggplot(data = diamonds) +
  geom_boxplot(mapping = aes(x = color, y = carat))

ggplot(data = diamonds) +
  geom_boxplot(mapping = aes(x = clarity, y = carat))
```
```{r}
ggplot(data = diamonds) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = carat, y = price), alpha = 0.1)
```
```{r}

diamonds2 <- diamonds |>
  filter(carat <= 2.5) |>
  mutate(lprice = log(price), lcarat = log(carat))

mod <- lm(lprice ~ lcarat, data = diamonds2)

diamonds2 <- diamonds2 |>
  add_predictions(mod) |>
  add_residuals(mod)

ggplot(data = diamonds2) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = lcarat, y = lprice), alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_line(mapping = aes(x = lcarat, y = pred), color = "red")
```


```{r}
mod2 <- lm(lprice ~ lcarat + cut + color + clarity, data = diamonds2)

broom::glance(mod)
broom::glance(mod2)
```


Recall that:

* best cut is Ideal, worst is Fair
* best color is D, worst is J
* best clarity is IF, worst is I1
